_comment: The stamped LINKED tier: how many matched translation units actually reach the
PC port's binary. This is a STAMP, not a live counter, and it cannot be anything
else from main: port/tools/linkage.py reads build/port/walk_window.map, which only
exists after an MSVC build of the port, and CI on main has no such build.
BEFORE STAMPING, LOOK FOR A BUILD THAT ALREADY EXISTS. Every port lane carries its
own build tree, so a current walk_window.map is usually already on disk:
ls -la */build/port/walk_window.map
across the port worktrees, newest first, then run the tool against that root. The
first version of this file was stamped off a five-day-old branch while a map from
the night before sat unread one directory away, and published 26.5% when the real
figure was 34.5%. A stale stamp is still a real measurement, just of the wrong run.
To refresh: run `python port/tools/linkage.py [root]` and update the numbers below
together with branch, commit and measuredAt. Never move the count without also
moving the provenance fields - tools/tiers.py drops a stamp missing any of them,
which is the intended behaviour for a number nobody can trace.
basis records what the figure is a measurement OF. The port branches are not merged,
so this is the best single lane rather than a combined total. All seven live lanes,
lk5 3819. Overlapping but not identical seats, so the merged figure is higher and
the published number stays a floor.
This number moves ONE way: seating a new actor class, worth ~8-10 TUs each.
Enrolling free TUs does nothing, because the release build dead-strips whatever the
linked closure never references.
basis: integration branch port/link100 at its pushed tip 2962e3ada, measured against that tip's own battery build walk_window.map (C:/tmp/l1-int, gate INT12: tree clean, battery ALL GREEN at floor 10147 with every minigame scene row green, six proofs green including the opening-cutscene gate), and confirmed by the hosted-runner port-linkage workflow, which counts every push of port/** and every pull request into the shipping branch on a GitHub Windows machine with no cartridge; since 2026-09-08 the shipping branch takes landings only through such pull requests, with the count required by a branch rule. +18 over the 2026-09-08 late stamp of 10145, +130 over that morning's 10033, +1042 over the 2026-08-30 stamp of 9121. Since the 10145 stamp: the ROM's own main runs as the port's boot spine by default (its two unrunnable callees, the game-init body with four refused arms and the game loop, are host seams the ROM's main really calls; the escape hatch is SM64DS_ROM_MAIN=0), the ten cutscene state dispatchers on their 69 cartridge-checked cells, the three tables whose extent the symbol table could not close (bounded by the delinks .bss span, seated over the maximum span with aborting slack cells), and three ov006 object-field rows whose pair universes a class-block sweep closes. Gated rungs since the last stamp: 10145 -> 10147 -> 10163. The pointer-to-member family is now closed except for 29 one-per-overlay object-field rows, two guess-marked bodies and one row that needs a run to prove its field is installed before dispatch; the boot plan's remaining rungs put +72 behind handing the frame to the ROM's own loop, and the wireless chain (~256 behind three documented gates) needs an ARM7 model.
